title: The Middle Passage
objective: After this level you can describe the Atlantic crossing enslaved Africans were forced to endure, and how many were carried to the Americas.
summary: SlaveVoyages estimates about 12.5 million Africans were forced aboard and 10.7 million survived. Equiano told of the crossing; captives revolted; about 388,000 landed in North America.

cards.headline: About 12.5 million people were forced aboard ships bound for the Americas.
cards.body: The Middle Passage was their crossing of the Atlantic. Here is what the records, and one survivor, tell us.

cards.headline: Counting a crossing
cards.body: Historians count the voyages with the SlaveVoyages database, built from shipping records. Its estimates: about 12.5 million Africans were forced aboard ships to the Americas, and about 10.7 million survived the crossing. The gap means roughly 1.8 million people died on the way.

cards.headline: Below deck
cards.body: Olaudah Equiano, once enslaved and later free, published an autobiography in 1789. He described captives kept below deck in chains and filth, amid “the shrieks of the women, and the groans of the dying.” His book gave readers something the ship records couldn’t: a survivor’s voice.

cards.headline: Fighting back
cards.body: Captives did not simply endure. They rose in revolt on about one slave ship in ten, most often while the ship was still near the African coast. Few of the revolts succeeded, but they show that captives fought back.

cards.headline: Where the ships went
cards.body: Most survivors were landed in the Caribbean and South America. About 388,000 were landed directly in mainland North America, a small share of the total.

mascot.line: Don’t memorize every figure. Remember the scale: millions carried, and only a small share to mainland North America.

cards.headline: The Middle Passage: explained
learned: About 12.5 million forced aboard; about 10.7 million survived

questions.prompt: According to SlaveVoyages estimates, about how many Africans survived the Middle Passage?

options.label: About 1.8 million
options.rationale: That’s roughly how many died on the way.

questions.explanation: About 12.5 million were forced aboard, and about 10.7 million survived.

questions.prompt: What does the record of shipboard revolts show about the captives?

options.label: They rarely resisted
options.rationale: Revolts hit about one ship in ten.

options.label: They resisted, rising up on about one ship in ten
They revolted only after landing
options.rationale: Most revolts came near the African coast.

questions.explanation: Captives rose in revolt on about one slave ship in ten.

questions.prompt: Level 14’s “20 and odd” Africans were among the first in English Virginia. About how many Africans in all were landed directly in mainland North America?

options.label: About 10.7 million
options.rationale: That’s the total for all the Americas.

options.label: About 5 million
options.rationale: Far too high; most went to the Caribbean and South America.

questions.explanation: About 388,000, a small share of the roughly 10.7 million who survived.
